name: OpenSchool
use_label: Run a school’s records in one system
one_liner: An open school platform: records, attendance, timetables, marks and reports in one place.

text.why: Many schools still run on paper and a handful of disconnected tools, which makes information hard to find, update and share safely. OpenSchool brings that work into one system a school can host itself, keeping student and administrative data under local control.
text.take: It began for Sri Lankan government schools, but the shape of it travels. The point is giving a public institution a way to run this without handing its records to a foreign commercial service.
build: A Go and Gin backend covering academic years, grades, classes and streams, student, staff and guardian records, daily attendance, curriculum and term marks with promotions, timetable planning and publishing, in-app notifications, reports and dashboards — with separate portals for administrators, teachers, students and parents. No licence fees, no vendor lock-in.

who.role: School administrators, public-sector and education bodies needing their own system, and people building education software.

start.text: Read the feature guide on the project site, then stand up a test install.

caveat: It is shaped around the Sri Lankan school system, so terms and marking need adapting elsewhere. With twenty-six stars it is early, and worth evaluating carefully before any real deployment.

license.scope_text: Commercial use, redistribution OK. Keep notices; mark changes.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
